text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovakia's state budget deficit totalled 17.9 billion crowns in the first seven months of this year.

- The share of engineering production in the steel producer VSZ Kosice is expected to reach 20 to 30 percent of the company's overall production within the next five years, up from the current 12 percent.
- Some 425 requests for political asylum have been registered in Slovakia since the beginning of this year. Slovakia granted asylum in 21 cases, while 150 requests are still under consideration.

- The trade union of the minining and oil producing industry has criticised the sell-off of major Slovak oil and gas storage company Nafta Gbely in 1996. One year after the privatisation people still do not know who are the real owners of Nafta Gbely, the trade union said.

SME - Deputy Chairman of the opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), Ivan Simko, said rulings approved by parliament after the governing coalition last December voted to withdraw the parliamentary mandate from Jozef Gaulieder, were illegal.
- Nafta Gbely General Director, Juraj Grebac, said he did not know who the real owners of the company are.
- Slovakia's sole tyre producer Matador Puchov said its profit totalled 70.7 million crowns in the first quarter of this year.

PRAVDA - The Slovak Democratic Coalition (SDK), grouping five main opposition parties, said it would initiate by the end of August an extraordinary parliamentary session to return the mandate to Jozef Gaulieder.

- The ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said there was no reason why the French far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen should not visit the Slovak parliament during his visit to the country in September.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Some 337,000 hectares, or around 47 percent of the overall sown land has been harvested so far this year, compared with 51 percent of the harvested area at the same time last year.
- One of Slovakia's major construction firms, Vahostav, said its foreign activities should account for 15 to 20 percent of overall production in the near future.
